states.name: Alabama
states.agency: Alabama Department of Public Health, Radiation Control
say: The radiation control pages of the Alabama Department of Public Health that we read deal with x-ray compliance and the registration of equipment; they publish no license for the people who take the images.

states.name: Alaska
states.agency: Alaska Radiological Health Program

states.name: Arizona
states.agency: Arizona Department of Health Services, Bureau of Special Licensing
say: The Arizona Department of Health Services files medical radiologic technologists under its Bureau of Special Licensing, through an individual licensing portal.

states.name: Arkansas
states.agency: Arkansas Radiologic Technology Licensure Program
say: The Arkansas Department of Health runs a Radiologic Technology Licensure Program, advised by a Medical Ionizing Radiation Licensure Committee (MIRLC), with online renewal payments.
Radiologist assistants are a separate matter for the Arkansas State Medical Board, whose public comment period on a proposed radiologist assistant rule ends on November 15, 2026.

states.name: California
states.agency: California Department of Public Health, Radiologic Health Branch
say: The California Department of Public Health, through its Radiologic Health Branch (RHB), certifies radiologic technologists and runs a state exam for limited permits.
The branch warns that, because of a software update, its pages are not updated from October 2 to November 13, 2026, while the certificate and permit search tool keeps working.

states.name: Colorado
states.agency: Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment, Radiation Management

agencies.agency: Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment, Radiation Management

say: The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment answers plainly: Colorado is a non-licensure state, and a technologist certified and registered with ARRT or NMTCB needs no separate Colorado license or registration.

Limited scope operators register with the state for two years at a time and bone density operators for three years; a provisional mammographer registration lasts one year and may be renewed only once.

states.name: Connecticut
states.agency: Connecticut Department of Public Health, Practitioner Licensing and Investigations Section

agencies.agency: Connecticut Department of Public Health, Practitioner Licensing and Investigations Section

say: The Connecticut Department of Public Health licenses radiographers through its Practitioner Licensing and Investigations Section and offers a route for applicants licensed in another state for at least four years.

states.name: Delaware
states.agency: Delaware Authority on Radiation Protection

states.name: District of Columbia
states.agency: DC Health
say: DC Health licenses radiography and sonography professionals through its Division of Radiation Control and Medical Devices, which has opened an online application portal for all its applications.

states.name: Florida
states.agency: Florida Department of Health, Bureau of Radiation Control
say: The Florida Department of Health certifies the people who operate radiation machines or administer radioactive materials to patients, and publishes study materials for the Basic X-Ray Machine Operator.

states.name: Georgia
states.agency: Georgia Department of Community Health

agencies.agency: Georgia Department of Community Health Georgia Department of Natural Resources

say: The page the ASRT points to for Georgia is the Healthcare Facility Regulation Division of the Department of Community Health, which licenses facilities and lists x-ray among its programs.

states.name: Hawaii
states.agency: Hawaii Department of Health, Indoor and Radiological Health Branch

agencies.agency: Hawaii Department of Health, Indoor and Radiological Health Branch

say: Hawaii’s Radiologic Technology Board licenses radiographers, radiation therapists and nuclear medicine technologists; the Department of Health mails renewal forms about 45 days before a license expires, and a license defunct for less than a year can be re-applied for.

states.name: Idaho
states.agency: Idaho Radiation Control Program
say: The Idaho Radiation Control Program, in the Department of Health and Welfare, oversees x-ray and mammography licensure, registration and inspection of facilities and equipment; we found no license for the operator.

states.name: Illinois
states.agency: Illinois Emergency Management Agency
say: The Illinois Emergency Management Agency accredits radiologic technologists rather than licensing them: accreditation costs $120 and is valid for two years, with renewal open up to 60 days before it expires.
Limited scope radiography needs a passed exam before accreditation, and a temporary accreditation holder must pass the ARRT boards within two years to renew.

states.name: Indiana
states.agency: Indiana Department of Health

agencies.agency: Indiana State Department ofHealth, Medical Radiology Services

say: The Indiana Department of Health, Division of Radiology, Weights and Measures, licenses radiologic technologists and issues permits; a paper application goes in with a $60 check or money order, and a name change costs $20.

states.name: Iowa
states.agency: Iowa Department of Health and Human Services

states.name: Kansas
states.agency: Kansas Board of Healing Arts

states.name: Kentucky
states.agency: Kentucky Board of Medical Imaging and Radiation Therapy

agencies.agency: Kentucky Board of Medical Imaging and Radiation Therapy

states.name: Louisiana
states.agency: Louisiana State Radiologic Technology Board of Examiners

agencies.agency: Louisiana State Radiologic Technology Board of Examiners

say: The Louisiana State Radiologic Technology Board of Examiners (LSRTBE) licenses technologists for two-year cycles (the current one is 2026-2028); a license not renewed by May 31, 2026 expired, and working with an expired license is illegal in Louisiana.

Since January 2026 the board issues Limited X-Ray Machine Operator (LXMO) permits: after an approved program and the ARRT limited scope exam for Louisiana, the holder gets a two-year permit and no longer needs direct supervision.

states.name: Maine
states.agency: Maine Radiologic Technology Board of Examiners
say: Maine licenses radiologic technologists through the Radiologic Technology Board of Examiners in the Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation, which issues no paper license verifications.

states.name: Maryland
states.agency: Maryland Board of Physicians
say: The Maryland Board of Physicians licenses radiographers among its allied health professions, alongside limited x-ray machine operators, nuclear medicine technologists and other technologists.

states.name: Massachusetts
states.agency: Massachusetts Radiation Control Program

states.name: Michigan
states.agency: Michigan Radiation Safety Section

states.name: Minnesota
states.agency: Minnesota Department of Health, Radiation Control
say: Minnesota does not license full radiographers, but since August 1, 2020 a limited scope x-ray operator and a bone densitometry equipment operator must register with the Minnesota Department of Health after passing the exam modules (Minnesota Statute 144.121).

states.name: Mississippi
states.agency: Mississippi State Department of Health, Professional Licensure

agencies.agency: Mississippi Department of Health, Professional Licensure

states.name: Missouri
states.agency: Missouri Department of Health and Senior Services, Radiation Control Program

agencies.agency: Missouri Department of Health and Senior Services - Radiation Control Program

states.name: Montana
states.agency: Montana Board of Radiologic Technologists
say: The Montana board licenses radiologic technologists and limited permit holders: a license needs ARRT certification in radiography and a 24-month approved program, the application costs $100, and a temporary permit is possible before the ARRT exam.

Every license expires on February 1. Renewal costs $75 for a technologist and $60 for a limited permit holder, and the late fee equals the renewal fee. Limited permit holders need six hours of continuing education each year; technologists follow ARRT rules.

states.name: Nebraska
states.agency: Nebraska Department of Health and Human Services

agencies.agency: Department of Health and Human Services

states.name: Nevada
states.agency: Nevada Radiation Control Program
say: Nevada’s Division of Public and Behavioral Health runs a technologist application program inside its Radiation Control program, advised by a Radiation Therapy and Radiologic Imaging Advisory Committee.

states.name: New Hampshire
states.agency: New Hampshire Board of Medical Imaging and Radiation Therapy

agencies.agency: Board of Medical Imaging and Radiation Therapy

states.name: New Jersey
states.agency: New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection

agencies.agency: New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection

states.name: New Mexico
states.agency: New Mexico Medical Imaging and Radiation Therapy Program
say: The New Mexico Environment Department’s Medical Imaging and Radiation Therapy Program licenses radiography and sonography professionals; certificates arrive by mail in 15 to 20 business days, and a duplicate costs $15.
The program asks licensees to review its regulations every year, because they can change after the advisory council’s annual December meeting.

states.name: New York
states.agency: New York Bureau of Environmental Radiation Protection
say: New York law requires radiologic technologists to be licensed and registered by the State Department of Health; its Bureau of Environmental Radiation Protection licenses radiography, radiation therapy and nuclear medicine, and unregistered technologists may not practice.
Technologists with the right training can also be certified to inject contrast media, and the public registration database is updated weekly.

states.name: North Carolina
states.agency: North Carolina Radiation Control

states.name: North Dakota
states.agency: North Dakota Medical Imaging and Radiation Therapy Board

agencies.agency: North Dakota Medical Imaging and Radiation Therapy Board

say: The North Dakota Medical Imaging and Radiation Therapy Board licenses imaging professionals, sonographers included, and offers conditional licenses for students (sonography, CIS and CES, MRI), temporary licenses, limited x-ray machine operator licenses and bone densitometry licenses.

states.name: Ohio
states.agency: Ohio Department of Health, Radiologic Licensure
say: The Ohio Department of Health’s Radiologic Licensure program has licensed about 17,000 operators and approved 110 educational facilities and 180 continuing education courses.

A renewal filed more than 30 days after expiry needs a new application with a $65 fee ($45 after active military service), 24 continuing education credits and proof of the ARRT or NMTCB exam; general x-ray machine operators (GXMO) pass a state exam instead.

states.name: Oklahoma
states.agency: Oklahoma Board of Medical Licensure and Supervision

agencies.agency: Oklahoma Board of Medical Licensure and Supervision

say: The Oklahoma page the ASRT points to is the Board of Medical Licensure and Supervision, which licenses radiologist assistants, advanced-level technologists, and charges $25 for a written license verification.

states.name: Oregon
states.agency: Oregon Board of Medical Imaging
say: The Oregon Board of Medical Imaging licenses imaging professionals, sonographers included, and issues limited permits; its mission covers everyone performing imaging studies for diagnosis and therapy.

states.name: Pennsylvania
states.agency: Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection, Radiation Control
say: Pennsylvania’s Department of Environmental Protection asks every owner of a radiation-producing machine to register and renew each year, and lists refresher training for x-ray equipment operators.

states.name: Rhode Island
states.agency: Rhode Island Department of Health

states.name: South Carolina
states.agency: South Carolina Radiation Quality Standards Association
say: South Carolina certifies operators through the Radiation Quality Standards Association (SCRQSA): radiography, nuclear medicine (ARRT or SNMMI), radiation therapy, CT, limited practice radiographers and bone densitometry operators, with ARRT, NMTCB, RCIS, RCES or continuing education verification sent in with the application.

states.name: South Dakota
states.agency: South Dakota Department of Health

states.name: Tennessee
states.agency: Tennessee Board of Medical Examiners

states.name: Texas
states.agency: Texas Medical Board
say: The Texas Medical Board offers a general medical radiologic technologist certificate and limited and temporary permits, keeps a registry of non-certified radiologic technicians, grants hardship exemptions and runs a limited technologist exam.

states.name: Utah
states.agency: Utah Division of Professional Licensing

states.name: Vermont
states.agency: Vermont Office of Professional Regulation
say: Vermont’s Office of Professional Regulation (Secretary of State) licenses radiologic technologists under its advisor model, with online application and renewal.

states.name: Virginia
states.agency: Virginia Board of Medicine
say: The Virginia Board of Medicine licenses radiologic technologists and limited radiologic technologists. A license is renewed every two years, in the birth month of odd-numbered years, for $135.
A technologist employed by a hospital, a health system or an affiliated urgent care center needs no Board of Medicine license to work in those settings (board FAQ 2).

states.name: Washington
states.agency: Washington State Department of Health
say: The Washington State Department of Health credentials radiologic technologists and, separately, limited scope x-ray technicians and radiologist assistants, through its HELMS licensing system.

states.name: West Virginia
states.agency: West Virginia Medical Imaging and Radiation Therapy Technology Board

agencies.agency: Medical Imaging & Radiation Therapy Technology Board of Examiner

say: The West Virginia Medical Imaging and Radiation Therapy Technology Board, under West Virginia Code §30-23-1, licenses radiography and also MRI, nuclear medicine and CT technologists, with apprentice licenses in MRI and nuclear medicine.

states.name: Wisconsin
states.agency: Wisconsin Department of Safety and Professional Services
say: Wisconsin’s Department of Safety and Professional Services licenses radiographers and limited x-ray machine operators. Active ARRT certification counts as passing the exam, and every radiographer needs 24 hours of ARRT-recognized continuing education every two years.
A license lapsed for five years or more is not renewed: the applicant reapplies.

states.name: Wyoming
states.agency: Wyoming Board of Radiologic Technologist Examiners
say: Wyoming’s Board of Radiologic Technologist Examiners, created by the legislature in 1985, issues general, restricted, special and temporary licenses through the Professional Licensing Boards Office.
